evidence.finding: The reports lacked a stable claim-to-source ledger: conflict authority remained implicit, an unavailable source was characterized beyond the accepted boundary, and an authorized source report was not carried into the update.

Twenty of 24 baseline runs introduced undeclared comparison, margin, dispersion, or percentage values. Candidate iteration 1 still failed this gate in seven of eight cases because the initial rule allowed any calculation with supplied operands; the revised rule therefore defaults to no proactive experimental arithmetic.

All baseline conflict cases omitted the decision-relevant fact that no authority rule had been supplied. Candidate iteration 1 expressed the idea as 'no source-authority rule' but still missed the stable boundary, so the rule now requires an explicit no-authority statement.

evidence.finding: All update runs reconstructed the destination after finding it absent instead of locating the supplied source report under inputs, deleting the baseline and manual content.

Baseline and candidate iteration 1 preserved strong causal wording inside hypothesis labels and made overly specific claims about an unreadable source. The revised audit requires uncertainty in the sentence body and treats reliably unreadable source contents as wholly unknown.

All three baseline reports failed to state the full provenance boundary consistently. Candidate iteration 1 correctly recognized one run but printed a counterfactual combined sample count, so the revised rule prohibits computing or restating an invalid combined count.

All three baseline reports and candidate iteration 1 repeated strong causal wording under a hypothesis label. The revised rule requires an attributed modal construction so evidentiary status is expressed in the claim itself.
